newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post record gains on bond rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post record gains on bond rally.

* Toronto stocks hit new highs on Wednesday, extending recent
record gains * Stocks aided by bond rally * Biggest gains in
transport, conglomerates * 130 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks posted another record close on Wednesday, following gains in New York and a rally in debt markets.
The TSE 300 Composite Index added 49.40 points to finish at 6850.57, its third straight record this week.
The key index also set a new intraday high of 6850.63.
"Buyers shined today. Bonds are doing well and every sub-index but communications was up today," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 80 points to reach its third consecutive all-time high.
Toronto's trading volume was heavier than recent sessions, totaling about 130 million shares worth C$1.8 billion.
Advancing stocks easily beat declines 611 to 419, with 266 issues unchanged.
Interest-rate sensitive stocks received a boost from today's rally in Canadian bonds. The 30-year long bond gained C$1 to 121.15 to yield 6.326 percent.
Banks, pipelines, transport and conglomerates were among the TSE's 13 strong sectors. The lone weak group was communications and media, down 53 points.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Toronto-Dominion Bank led active bank stocks, adding 0.75 to 43.85 on 2.3 million shares. Several banks lowered long-term mortgage rates on Wednesday, while short-term rates have climbed recently amid expectations that the Bank of Canada would raise interest rates to prop up a weak dollar.
* Laidlaw Inc closed up 0.25 at 21.55 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 21.60 on news of Laidlaw's US$400 million acquisition of U.S. health care transportation firm EmCare Holdings.
* Lafarge Corp led net gainers, up 5.25 to 44.25, a 52-week high, but the firm could not explain the activity.
